title: Rear Seat Cushion Removal and Installation
introduction:
The rear seat cushion is held to the floor by locking tabs at its front edge. I treat those tabs like a suitcase latch: release the catch before lifting the lid. Pulling harder can damage the very pieces that hold the cushion down.

This job moves both front seats forward for access, releases the cushion and reverses that sequence for installation. Before finishing, give the seatbelts their own check: untwisted webbing and accessible buckles matter as much as getting the cushion back into place.

items.name: Prevent an unexpected start
items.detail: Park on level ground with the parking brake applied and wheels chocked; keep P selected on an automatic or a parked gear on a manual. Keep the engine stopped throughout. Disable remote start, if equipped, through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before dismantling anything. Otherwise, someone could remotely start the car, causing personal injury or death. If the setting needs ignition power, keep the valid intelligent access key inside. From confirmed OFF, press and release START/STOP without pressing either pedal to select engine-off ON. If already ON for the settings, leave it ON rather than toggling it. After the setting change, return ON to OFF by pressing and releasing the button without pressing a pedal; if already OFF, leave it OFF. With the ignition OFF, remove the key from the vehicle before service to prevent another person from starting the engine; an accidental start may cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Protect eyes, ears and hands
items.detail: Wear eye and ear protection during vehicle service. Wear protective gloves when handling parts with pointed or sharp edges. Ignoring these precautions can cause serious personal injury. Review the applicable [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189) before beginning.

items.name: Position the front seats before cushion work
items.detail: Keep everyone and all objects clear of the seat travel; never adjust the driver seat while the vehicle is moving. Move both front seats fully forward using their fitted controls. For manual seats, lift the bar beneath the front of the cushion, slide the seat forward, release the bar and rock the seat backward and forward to confirm that it locks. For power seats, move the outboard seat-control switch forward. If power is needed, bring the valid key inside and use the confirmed OFF-to-engine-off-ON sequence above without pressing either pedal. Once the seats are positioned, return any known ON state to OFF using the button with both pedals released; leave a state already OFF alone. With the ignition OFF, remove the key from the vehicle before releasing the rear cushion.

edits.text: Move both front seats fully forward.
edits.why: Moving each front seat out of the way creates access to the front edge of the rear cushion and its floor attachments. Use the fitted seat controls and power-state sequence in preparation before releasing the rear-cushion tabs.

edits.text: NOTICE: Press the seat cushion locking tabs inward before lifting the cushion away from the floor. Trying to release the cushion without pressing the tabs can damage them.
edits.why: The tabs are catches that must be released; lifting force alone is not the release mechanism.

edits.text: Find the locking tabs beneath the front edge of the rear seat cushion, at the attachment locations shown on each side of the illustration. Press the tabs inward to release the cushion from the floor.
edits.why: I locate the catches before pulling on the upholstery. The inset shows the movable latch, while the wider view identifies where to reach along the cushion's front edge.

edits.text: With the front locking tabs released, lift the cushion to free it from its installed position, then remove it from the vehicle.
edits.why: The cushion should be released from its attachments before it is carried out; the blue illustration identifies the complete cushion being removed.

edits.text: NOTE: During installation, keep the seatbelt webbing untwisted and leave the seatbelts and buckles accessible to the occupant.
edits.why: A cushion can look neatly installed while trapping a buckle underneath it. I check the belts as the cushion goes back, before access becomes awkward.

edits.text: Reverse the removal sequence: return the cushion to its installed position, lower it into place and re-engage the front locking tabs with their floor attachments. Keep the seatbelts and buckles accessible as you position the cushion, then return the front seats from their fully forward access positions.
edits.why: Reversing the sequence restores the cushion's attachments as well as its position. The finishing check is an attached cushion with untwisted, accessible belts and buckles. Restore the front seats using the same fitted controls: for manual seats, lift the front bar, slide to the required position, release and rock to confirm locking; for power seats, move the outboard switch backward as required with everyone and all objects clear. If power is needed, bring the key inside and select engine-off ON only from confirmed OFF, with both pedals released. After positioning, return known ON to OFF with the button and both pedals released; do not toggle a state already OFF. With the ignition OFF, remove the key from the vehicle. Keep the car parked and restrained throughout, and do not use a seat that is not securely retained.

editorialRevision.scope: Actual manual/power seat controls, stationary setup and coordinated final OFF; primary cushion action text unchanged. Pending independent increment review.
